2D cel-shaded anime, studio-quality animation, flat shading, shoujo, high school, reverse harem, romance, comedy, fictional characters, NO MUSIC.

Setting:

The corridor of an ordinary Japanese high school.

Scenario:

The second part of a character introduction scene between Juri and one of the love interests (Shun). The interaction is comedic and has the timing of a shoujo romantic comedy.

SHOT 1 — THE MYSTERIOUS HAND:

Frame 1 start on this frame.

Medium shot: Juri is sitting on the ground after falling over, looking slightly dazed. A handsome young man's hand reaches down into frame, offered to help her up. Juri looks at the hand, then up towards the unseen person.

SHOT 2 — THE REVEAL

Close-up on Juri's hand taking the young man's hand.

Medium shot: Young man gently pulls Juri to her feet.

Close-up of Shun, Reveal Shun's handsome face. He smiles apologetically.

Shun: "Oh, sorry! Didn't see you there."

As he finishes speaking, he casually flips his long hair in glorious, exaggerated slow motion. His hair catches the light. The camera briefly treats him like the most handsome boy in the world.

SHOT 3 — JURI'S BRAIN STOPS WORKING

Juri stares at Shun, completely mesmerised. Her eyes widen and sparkle. Her mouth hangs open.

Juri: "Wooooooooooooow..."

She begins making increasingly incoherent, flustered noises.

Juri: "Hum-a-nuh, hum-a-nuh, hum-a-nuh, hum-a-nuh! BRRRR!"

She shakes her head vigorously side-to-side in a cartoonish manner, trying desperately to regain her composure.

Juri: "You're hot... I mean, you're handsome... I mean, you're Juri, *I'M* Juri... Damnit..." (emphasis on the word "I'm")

Juri's confidence completely collapses. She lowers her head, looking embarrassed and slightly ashamed of herself, unable to believe what just came out of her mouth.

SHOT 4 — SHUN MAKES IT WORSE

Shun chuckles warmly, completely relaxed and unbothered.

Shun: "No worries. I kinda have that effect on girls."

He gives her a charming smile.

Shun: "Hey, you're pretty cute yourself."

SHOT 5 — TOTAL SYSTEM FAILURE

Juri freezes.

Juri's face turns bright red, starting at her neck and rapidly spreads upwards across her face, all the way to the top of her head. Use an exaggerated cartoon anime blush effect, as if her entire head is overheating.

Her eyes widen, then soften. She lets out a tiny, involuntary giggle.

Juri:"Hehehehehe..."

She giggles like a lovestruck schoolgirl, completely unlike her usual confident, mischievous self. She clasps her hands close to her chest, utterly smitten.

SHOT 6 — THE PERFECT EXIT

Shun smiles and turns away.

Shun: "Well, see you around."

He turns and walks away in ridiculously smooth, cinematic slow motion, his hair flowing dramatically as though he's starring in a romance film.

The camera follows him for a moment, presenting him as effortlessly cool.

CRASH!

Shun walks directly into a wall.

He pauses, slightly dazed. He scratches the back of his head with an embarrassed grin, then casually continues walking as if nothing happened.

Juri remains in the background, still blushing and giggling, completely oblivious to his embarrassing exit.

FINAL COMEDIC CONTRAST: Juri thinks she has just met the most perfect boy in existence. Shun is, in fact, a handsome dork.

A mostly sweet, youthful feminine voice with a subtle natural rasp that adds warmth and edge. She speaks with confident energy and a hint of playfulness, but her tone can flip into a sharp, biting snap when her tsundere side flares up, especially when she is flustered or trying to hide affection. No accent, clean English dub style.

Youthful, warm, medium-high masculine voice; charming, princely and slightly theatrical, with expressive romantic inflections and playful confidence. Naturally flirtatious, cheerful and gentlemanly, but endearingly airheaded. Smooth, exaggerated delivery for dramatic moments, yet sincere and relaxed in casual conversation. Tamaki Suoh-esque romantic-comedy energy.

p:
【映像プロンプト／サイバーパンクの酒場・続きのシーン・アニメ・15秒】

■基本設定
映像の総尺は厳密に15秒。以下の時間指定は完成映像上の再生時間。前シーンの直後から始まり、ファルカーメンの忠告、ギャングの攻撃、片手による制止と投擲、テーブルへの激突、別のギャングによる銃の威嚇、店内の人々の恐怖、動じないファルカーメンまでを描く。
劇場版クオリティのサイバーパンクアニメ。力強く整った人物作画、精密な背景、立体的なセル調の陰影。青緑とマゼンタのネオン、カウンターの琥珀色の照明が、黒い仮面、肌、酒瓶、グラスへ反射する。静かな会話から一瞬の激しい動きへ切り替わり、最後は張り詰めた静けさへ戻る。

前シーンと同じ酒場、カウンター、家具の配置、バーテンダー、一般客、パンクなギャングたちを維持する。ファルカーメンはすでにカウンター席から立ち上がっており、ギャングたちに向き直っている。立ち上がる動作や入店を繰り返さない。注文したミルクはまだ提供されていない。

■キャラクターと位置関係
画像1をファルカーメンの外見参照とする。非常に筋肉質な上半身、青緑色の腰布、素足、黒い角付き仮面。仮面の複数の瞳状の発光部は、すべて終始緑色に輝く。仮面の形状、角、体格、露出した口元を一貫させる。

参照画像の全身像と顔のアップは、同じ一人のキャラクターを示す資料として扱う。映像に登場するファルカーメンは一人だけ。資料の白背景、文字、分割構図は使用しない。
ファルカーメンの背後にカウンター、正面と左右にギャングたち。ギャングの背後には酒瓶とグラスが置かれた無人のテーブルがある。投げ飛ばされる方向とテーブルの位置を、攻撃前から画面内で示す。

前シーンで仮面を殴って右手を痛めた男は、今回も右手を押さえたまま周囲に残る。今回殴りかかるのは、両手に負傷のない別のギャング。後半で銃を構える男も、投げ飛ばされる男とは別人とし、それぞれ髪型と衣装で明確に区別する。

■0.00～3.40秒：冷静な忠告
ファルカーメンを胸から上のミディアムショットで捉える。手前にギャングたちの肩を配置し、取り囲まれていることを示す。

ファルカーメンは仮面をゆっくり左右へ向け、周囲を見回しながら、落ち着いた声で日本語の台詞を言う。

ファルカーメン：
「暴力はいけない。店に迷惑だ」
相手を諭すような、静かではっきりした口調。「暴力はいけない」の後に短く間を置き、「店に迷惑だ」と続ける。怒鳴らず、挑発する笑みも浮かべない。口元を日本語の発音に自然に同期させる。

声質は前の注文シーンと同じ、既出の音声ファイル1を参照したファルカーメンの声を維持する。

カメラがわずかに横へ移動し、忠告を聞いて眉をつり上げるギャングたちの表情を背景に見せる。
■3.40～4.70秒：逆上するギャング
両手に負傷のないギャングが、顔を怒りでゆがめ、一歩踏み込む。周囲の仲間も苛立ち、前へ身を乗り出す。

攻撃するギャングが日本語で叫ぶ。

ギャング：
「ふざけんじゃねぇ！」

叫びの終わりに合わせて右拳を引き、そのままファルカーメンの顔へ向けてパンチを繰り出す。後ろのギャングたちは取り囲む位置を保ち、主となる攻防を隠さない。

カメラを斜め側面へ切り替え、攻撃する右腕とファルカーメンの上半身を同時に収める。
■4.70～6.00秒：片手だけで攻撃を止める
ファルカーメンは一歩も後退せず、左手だけを短く動かす。向かってくる男の右手首付近を左手で確実につかみ、拳が仮面へ届く前に止める。

攻撃していた腕が途中で止まり、男の肩と胴体だけが前へ流れかける。勢いのあるパンチが片手で完全に制止されたことを、身体の反応で見せる。

ファルカーメンの左肘と肩は安定し、表情は冷静なまま。右腕は身体の横へ自然に下ろし、補助に使わない。防御する瞬間だけ、つかんだ左手と男の右手首へカメラを寄せ、接触を明確にする。
■6.00～7.50秒：同じ片手で投げ飛ばす
ファルカーメンは相手の右手首をつかんだ左手を離さず、腰を小さく回す。圧倒的な腕力で男の身体を横方向の弧に乗せ、そのまま後方の無人テーブルへ投げ飛ばす。

男の両足が床を離れ、胴体が先に引かれ、脚とジャケットの裾が遅れて大きく振られる。男の身体全体が宙へ出たところでファルカーメンの左手が離れ、投げられた勢いのままテーブルへ飛んでいく。

「左手で右手首をつかむ→同じ左手で身体を振る→両足が浮く→手を離す→男が飛ぶ」という動作を連続して描く。両手で持ち上げたり、蹴りや別のパンチを追加したりしない。

カメラはファルカーメンの腰の高さから投擲の弧に沿って素早くパンし、男の身体を追う。ファルカーメン本人はほぼ元の場所に残る。
■7.50～9.40秒：テーブルへ激突、瓶とグラスが宙を舞う
投げ飛ばされた男が、背中と肩からテーブルへ激突する。天板が大きくたわみ、脚が折れ、身体とともにテーブルが崩れる。

衝突の直前まで天板に載っていたグラスと酒瓶が、衝撃を受けて一斉に宙へ跳ね上がる。透明なグラスが回転し、酒瓶が横向きに舞い、酒のしぶきがネオンを反射しながら広がる。飛び出す向きや回転速度をそれぞれ変え、立体的で重量感のある散乱にする。

カメラはテーブルの斜め横から、男の衝突、浮き上がる食器、崩れる天板を同じ画面で捉える。衝突時だけ短く振動し、宙を回る一本の酒瓶とグラスを一瞬鮮明に見せた後、床へ落下する動きを追う。

瓶とグラスの一部が床で砕け、破片と酒が周囲に散る。男は壊れたテーブルの中へ落ちて動きを止める。流血や傷口は描かず、家具の破壊と落下音で衝撃を表現する。

鋭い破砕音が残る中、別のギャングへカット。

仲間が投げ飛ばされたことに逆上した男が拳銃を取り出し、ファルカーメンへ向けて構える。銃を握る腕には力が入り、肩が上がり、顔には怒りと焦りが混じっている。

銃口をファルカーメンへ向けながら、日本語で叫ぶ。

銃を構えたギャング：
「ぶっ殺してやる！」

台詞は一度だけ、明瞭に発声する。銃を構えた男はその場に立ち、銃口をファルカーメンへ向け続ける。発砲はしない。
カメラは男の斜め横から銃と顔を捉え、その先に立つファルカーメンも画面奥へ入れる。銃口が誰へ向いているかを明確にする。

■11.50～12.80秒：店の隅へ縮こまる人々
酒場の隅を捉えた短いカット。

わずかに残っていた一般客が、壁際のボックス席の陰へ身を寄せ、頭を低くして縮こまる。バーテンダーもカウンター端の開口部から、そのすぐ横の隅へ身をかがめて退避する。人物が瞬間移動せず、近い位置にある遮蔽物へ逃げる動きを見せる。

客たちは肩を寄せ合い、腕で頭をかばいながら、銃を構えた男の様子を恐る恐るうかがう。バーテンダーは身体を小さくし、息をひそめる。追加の台詞は入れない。

背景には壊れたテーブル、倒れたギャング、床に散った瓶とグラスが残っている。
■12.80～15.00秒：銃口を前に動じないファルカーメン
銃を構えた男の肩越しのショット。画面手前に銃口と腕、画面奥の中央にファルカーメンが立つ。カメラがゆっくりファルカーメンへ寄り、焦点を銃から黒い仮面へ移す。

ファルカーメンは向けられた銃へ静かに視線を定め、まっすぐ見据える。仮面の緑色の発光部は一定の明るさを保ち、露出した口元にも動揺はない。両腕を自然に下ろし、背筋を伸ばしたまま動かない。

最後は、画面端にぼけた銃口を残し、ファルカーメンの仮面と落ち着いた口元を鮮明に捉える。ギャングの荒い呼吸、ネオン設備の低い駆動音、床へ落ちる最後の小さな破片だけが響く。

発砲、弾丸、回避、反撃へは進めず、銃を向けられても揺るがないファルカーメンとの対峙で、15秒ちょうどに終了する。
■音声・BGM
ファルカーメンの台詞は落ち着いた声、最初に攻撃するギャングの台詞は怒りを露わにした声、銃を構える別の男の台詞は怒りと焦りが混じった声。それぞれ話者を明確に分け、日本語の口の動きと同期させる。三つの台詞を重ねず、指定の言葉を正確に発声する。

Create a 10-second animated slice-of-life shopping vlog, filmed as though the female inventor’s friend casually brought a small camcorder into a neighborhood grocery shop.

CHARACTER AND VISUAL WORLD
Use the attached female character sheet as the identity reference. Its panels depict ONE woman. Preserve her exact face, auburn curls, skin tone, teal work jacket, ivory undershirt, trousers and brass LEFT-forearm instrument throughout.

Keep the established painterly animation aesthetic: sculpted dimensional faces, angular facial planes, expressive hand-painted textures, visible brushwork, indigo shadow colors and restrained copper highlights. Every object and environment belongs to the same animated world.

Layer a subtle early-2000s home-video recording texture over the animation: mild image softness, faint digital noise, modest exposure adjustments and small handheld imperfections. Keep her face and acting readable.

LOCATION
A tiny neighborhood grocery tucked into an old brick industrial district. Narrow wooden shelves hold paper-wrapped groceries, jars, bread and simple unbranded snack packets. An aged glass refrigerator glows pale turquoise. Afternoon light enters through the shopfront, mixing with ordinary warm ceiling bulbs.

The refrigerator stands beside a small wooden counter near the entrance. Keep these landmarks consistent. The shop is quiet and contains no other visible people.

FIRST FRAME
The woman already stands beside the refrigerator, facing her friend behind the camera. She holds a small wire shopping basket in her RIGHT hand at hip height. One paper-wrapped loaf rests inside. A sealed strawberry pudding cup with a pale pink foil lid sits on the refrigerator shelf within reach of her LEFT hand.

THREE SHOTS — EXACTLY 10 SECONDS

0.0–3.2s — THE PROMISE
Eye-level medium shot with a gentle handheld drift, as though her friend has just stopped walking.

She tells the person filming:
“Just the essentials today.”

Her goal is to get her friend to believe she has a sensible plan. While finishing the sentence, she notices the pudding beside her. Her attention lingers on it before returning to the lens, checking whether her distraction was noticed.

The camera stays on her long enough to catch that small betrayal of the plan.

HARD CUT.

3.2–6.2s — THE EXCEPTION
A slightly closer three-quarter view from the same side, showing her face, LEFT hand and refrigerator shelf. One small handheld reframe follows her hand.

With her LEFT hand, she picks up the pudding cup and holds it beside her face, foil lid still attached. The basket remains in her RIGHT hand, low beside her body.

She tells her friend:
“These are technically essential.”

She presents the cup as evidence, trying to win agreement. Hold a brief listening beat afterward: she studies the person behind the lens to see whether the excuse worked. A tiny, restrained camera dip suggests her friend looking from her face to the dessert.

HARD CUT.

6.2–10.0s — THE DEFENSE
Frontal medium close-up, pudding visible near her chest in her LEFT hand. The refrigerator remains behind her on the same side. A very small, imperfect push-in from the camera operator emphasizes her explanation.

She says:
“Well... pudding has milk in it. Close enough!”

Begin as a sincere attempt to justify the purchase. On “Close enough,” she recognizes how weak her argument sounds, abandons the defense and shares a brief laugh with her friend. The camera gives a small responsive wobble as its operator chuckles.

End abruptly while she is still holding the pudding and starting to turn toward the counter. No fade or frozen pose.

ACTING TASK
Shared direction: enjoy a small everyday errand together.

Her personal goal is to persuade her friend that the treat belongs in a practical shopping trip. The obstacle is that she knows the excuse is transparent. First establish credibility, then sell the exception, then let her friend in on the joke.

Direct every spoken line toward the person immediately behind the lens. Her gaze checks whether the argument has landed; pauses contain listening and reconsideration. Keep facial movement specific and restrained rather than broad cartoon reactions. Natural blinks, no fixed smile or vacant stare.

VOICE AND SOUND
One warm female voice, casual conversational English, lightly dry humor and accurately synchronized lips. Deliver each line entirely within its assigned shot, with room for the reaction beats. Only the woman speaks. Her friend gives one quiet off-camera chuckle at the end.

Refrigerator hum, faint street sounds, gentle packaging rustle and a small basket creak. Slightly compressed camcorder microphone texture. No music, narration or additional voices.

CONTINUITY
One woman throughout. The basket stays in her RIGHT hand; the pudding moves from the shelf to her LEFT hand and stays there. Her forearm instrument remains attached to her LEFT forearm. One loaf in the basket, one pudding cup, consistent packaging and wardrobe. Fingers grip objects with visible contact; no floating, duplication or objects passing through hands.

No subtitles, text overlays, timestamps, logos or watermarks.

The only new end action is Lisa’s right hand moving to grip the personal spoon beside B, with the spoon bowl still resting at the plate edge. All food remains on its original plates.

[Performance Rules]
Before the clip begins, Lisa has already prepared all three meals and is trying to hold order together through the small act of straightening the third plate. “I made three portions again.” refers to the serving having already happened earlier; it must not trigger any new serving action. At the opening she is already tired and slightly red-eyed but not yet audibly crying. Her gaze moves from the food to the empty chair, then back to the third plate. She pauses. Moisture gathers at the lower eyelids. She tries to press her lips together and control her breath, but loses control midway through one inhale. The crying comes from chest and throat; lips part naturally for breathing; face shape stays intact; no wide-mouthed wailing or head-thrown-back sobbing. After the break, there are only two clearly visible shoulder/back jolts; the rest is small, irregular breath movement. After Alin touches her, Lisa does not stop crying instantly; she first registers the warmth on the back of her hand, then looks up to find Alin. By the end she has only earned one slightly longer exhale; tears and residual sobbing remain.

Alin’s objective is to bring Lisa back to the presence beside her and gently move her toward taking even one bite. She is also exhausted. Hearing Lisa cry, her jaw tightens briefly and her eyes moisten. She first adjusts one breath for herself, then chooses to reach out. Each close-up should carry one main change only: restraining breath, starting the reach, waiting for eye contact, softening the gaze. Keep subtle eye-target shifts and natural blinks, with reflections motivated by real lamp position, never glassy staring. She does not perform stoic slogans or fake smiles. Her hand stays quiet on Lisa’s hand. Their reactions are staggered: Lisa breaks first, Alin is affected second, Lisa is then influenced by Alin’s steadier breathing. No synchronized blinks, synchronized tears, or mechanical nodding.

[Voices and Dialogue]
Lisa, the short-haired leather-jacket woman from Image 2: adult female, natural mid-high register, soft with slight breathiness, clear natural English; crying gradually damages breath support but never stretches every syllable.
Alin, the long-haired white-top woman from Image 1: adult female, natural mid-low register, gentle English with chest support, quiet but clear; line endings tremble slightly when containing grief, and become softer in comfort, never lecture-like.
Voice identity, accent, and age stay stable across cuts. Only the designated speaker speaks in each line. Lisa’s soft nonverbal crying may continue under Alin’s dialogue but must not cover the words.

Use only these six lines, once each, at the assigned points:
Lisa: “Hia…”
Lisa: “I made three portions again.”
Alin: “I miss her too.”
Alin: “We need to stay strong.”
Alin: “Eat a little…”
Alin: “We still have to get out—together.”
The ellipsis and dash indicate short pauses only, not extra words. All dialogue is natural real-time speech. Pauses belong to breath and eye contact, not time-compressed dubbing.

[Look, Palette, and Light]
Grade the whole piece as realistic survival drama: low-saturation warm tungsten interior, gray-brown ruin materials, preserved skin tone, continuing the warm lamp and old textures from Image 3.
Palette direction only, never shown as text:
coal black #282624 for deep structure and shadow,
weathered wood brown-gray #665548 for table, chairs, and walls,
dark moss olive #555647 for sofa and background,
restrained amber #BA8C53 for lamp warmth and metal reflections,
old ivory #D9D0C1 for the lit planes of Alin’s white top.
Keep Lisa’s jacket orange-brown but reduce harsh saturation; keep natural blood in skin; blonde hair must not bleach to white.

The hanging lamp is the fixed world light source, around 3000–3200K tungsten. Overall white-balance direction is around 3800K so the lamp stays warm while faces do not turn orange. Walls and table provide weak natural bounce, preserving detail in the shadow side of eyes, mouth corners, and fingers. When camera angle changes, light direction changes according to real space only. Shadows stay neutral gray-brown, dense but never crushed. Highlights roll softly, preserving white-shirt wrinkles and forehead texture. Exposure, saturation, black level, and grain remain constant through the whole clip. After the comfort begins, the light must not become warmer, brighter, or emotionally “improved.” Keep a slight fine grain and a small halo around the lamp, without skin-smoothing or oversharpening; eyes and hands remain clear.

[Material Physics and Environment]
Everything obeys contact, gravity, and real material response. Lisa’s leather jacket forms brief elbow creases when she lifts her arm and naturally settles afterward; sobbing causes tiny delayed movement at shoulder seams and shearling collar; the leather keeps weight and thickness, and the waist cinch limits large torso bending. When Alin leans in, the white camisole compresses into waist folds, straps stay in place, and the jeans hold stable weight creases at the hips. Sleeves, forearms, and table edges create light friction and contact shadows. Clothes never clip through the table, never change design, and never respond to nonexistent indoor wind. Lisa’s short hair lags slightly when she lowers her head, then settles. Alin’s long hair moves softly with small head turns and never hides the eyes.

Tears first collect at the lower lids, then slide slowly down the real slope of the cheeks, leaving narrow irregular wet tracks. These tracks must persist across later shots; never reset to a dry face, never create floating droplets or glamour tear highlights. When Alin’s hand lands, it creates a slight skin compression and soft contact shadow. Finger count, joints, and wrist connections stay stable.
All meat is already on the three plates and stays stable. Only C produces a very shallow gravy ripple during the one slight adjustment, then settles. A and B remain still. No dropping, flying-in food, multiplication, or liquid changes.
Only a few floating dust particles exist in the room, briefly visible near the hanging lamp when caught by backlight, then disappearing into shadow. No new dust burst, no smoke layer, no face-covering haze. Dust belongs mainly to the establishing shot; face close-ups prioritize skin, eyes, and tear tracks.

[25-Second Seven-Shot Timeline]
00:00–00:04, Shot 1, 35mm feel, fixed medium-wide, high oblique about 45 degrees from the northwest side, with enough depth of field to cover the whole table.
The first frame must clearly show the complete A plate in front of Alin, the complete B plate in front of Lisa, and the complete C plate in front of the far empty chair, all three matching meals already plated and readable with no major blockage. Hold about one second so the viewer can read the relationship between two women and three meals. Then Lisa’s left fingertips nudge the already-set C plate about 1 cm. Her right hand stays empty beside B’s spoon. Her gaze rises from C to the empty chair. Her left hand freezes on the rim. Alin stays still in her opening pose, looking down at A. One short, quiet plate-on-wood sound only. Cut on the moment Lisa’s motion stops while her fingertips are still at the rim.

00:04–00:06, Shot 2, low close shot about 15 cm above the tabletop, looking toward the south-side empty chair.
Camera locked. Perform only one smooth rack focus: from the already-full C plate rim and Lisa’s fingertips into the empty chair back behind it. A and B still exist in place but are out of frame for this lens choice only. Lisa releases the rim and slides her left hand back along the tabletop to settle palm-down near the northwest corner. Her right hand remains empty beside her own plate. Hold one short beat on the empty chair in focus. Around 00:05.1–00:05.8, Lisa softly says off-screen, “Hia…,” as if still waiting for her to come take the meal. Let the tail fall into nothing. Room tone continues. Cut into Lisa’s eyes receiving the emptiness; do not repeat the call.

00:06–00:11.5, Shot 3, 85mm feel, Lisa eye-level three-quarter profile close-up, keeping jawline and shoulders.
For about the first three seconds, push in extremely slowly around 15 cm, then hold. Lisa’s eyes stay on the empty chair, then drop to the third meal. Moisture gathers at the lower eyelids. Around 00:06.3–00:08.7 she quietly says, “I made three portions again.” The first part tries to stay level; “again” lands gently. She presses her lips together afterward and tries to finish an inhale, but the breath breaks in the middle; support drops from the lower lip and the first audible sob leaks out on the exhale. In the latter part of the shot, tears travel down her cheeks, her head dips slightly, and the shoulders/back produce two uneven jolts. After the line, her mouth only opens and closes naturally for crying and breath; no extra words. Both hands stay in their table positions. She does not cover her face or wipe tears. Hold long enough to capture one post-break inhale. Cut away while the crying continues.

00:11.5–00:14, Shot 4, 85mm feel, Alin eye-level face close-up, locked, looking screen-right.
Lisa’s crying continues as a sound bridge. Alin’s jaw tightens briefly, her eyes wet up, and she lets out a small controlled exhale. Around 00:11.9–00:13.4 she quietly says, “I miss her too.” Let the tail of “too” tremble slightly. Then her gaze drops from Lisa’s face toward Lisa’s left hand on the table, and her right shoulder begins a small forward shift that initiates the reach with the right forearm. Her left hand stays on her thigh. Cut as the right forearm has already begun moving, so the next shot continues the same reach rather than restarting it.

00:14–00:16.5, Shot 5, fixed close overhead at roughly 45 degrees on the two hands, with a short section of both forearms included.
Alin’s right hand continues entering from frame left; Lisa’s left hand remains palm-down on frame right. Alin’s fingertips touch the back of Lisa’s hand first, then the palm settles gently over it and stays. Lisa’s fingers remain slightly curled at first, then relax a little after half a beat. No hand flip, no finger interlacing. This shot does only the contact: no stroking, no patting. Sound emphasizes a small fabric friction and the still-continuing sobbing. Cut after the contact has fully stabilized.

00:16.5–00:21, Shot 6, 65mm feel, level close shot focused on Alin, with Lisa’s soft out-of-focus side face and shoulder in the right foreground, locked.
After being touched, Lisa first lifts her eyes, then makes a small turn to find Alin. Alin waits until real eye contact exists before releasing tension in her jaw. Around 00:17.0–00:18.9 she says quietly, “We need to stay strong.” Let “we” include both of them; “strong” must not sound scolding. After a short beat, around 00:19.3–00:20.5 she says more softly, “Eat a little…” Her brow still carries slight tension, her eyes remain wet, and her gaze stays near Lisa’s eyes. Only after the line does she glance briefly down toward Lisa’s own plate, then back to Lisa. Their joined hands continue off-screen. Lisa’s shoulder slowly softens a little in the foreground under Alin’s calmer breathing, but she still has residual sobbing and does not give a mechanical nod. No extra gesture, no smile. Cut into the two-shot while preserving the same comfort moment.

00:21–00:25, Shot 7, 40mm feel, northwest-side two-shot medium, Alin left and Lisa right, with hands and the full table meal zone visible low in frame. A, B, and C are all visible again in their correct seat relationship, and the empty chair sits in the far middle-background.
Composition must prioritize keeping both A and B visible rather than blocked by forearms. For the first two seconds, the camera slides about 15 cm west while staying on the same axis side, so the forearms no longer overlap and the joined hands become clearly readable, then it locks off. Around 00:21.0–00:23.5 Alin continues, “We still have to get out—together.” Pause only briefly after “get out,” and let “together” land softly. Lisa keeps looking at Alin; when she hears “together,” she lets out one slightly longer exhale, though the residual crying remains. Around 00:23.5–00:25, Lisa lowers her eyes to her own plate, moves her right hand from beside the plate to the personal spoon, touches it, then grips the handle and holds it through the end. No extra pause and no second action. The spoon bowl stays against the plate edge, making only one light metal sound. She does not lift the spoon or eat. Alin’s right hand continues covering Lisa’s left hand, and her gaze follows the spoon-grip action. Her left hand remains on her thigh. Final live image: Lisa holding the spoon handle, tear tracks still visible, their other hands still joined, and the third meal still untouched. End naturally, no fade to black.

[Sound, Rhythm, and Continuity]
The soundtrack contains only the specified English dialogue, low room air through pipes, normal breathing, Lisa’s irregular sobbing, light metal contact on wood and tray, and small cloth friction. No extra dialogue, narration, lyrics, or background voices. Dialogue is the primary sound during the comfort passage; room tone and sobbing may soften slightly but never cut to silence. No music. Rhythm is driven by real breathing.
At the opening there is only the slight scrape of C being straightened; no scooping meat, pouring food, or serving-spoon contact with the can. Once Lisa breaks, the crying becomes the near-field sound focus, continuing through shots 4 and 5, then easing during the comfort passage without disappearing abruptly. Cloth sounds occur only when actual friction happens. Dust makes no sound.
Structure of rhythm:
first 4 seconds establish the three ready meals,
4–6 seconds suspend on the empty place,
6–11.5 seconds move from restraint into breakdown,
11.5–16.5 seconds turn through reaction and touch,
last 8.5 seconds settle through sustained eye contact, one longer exhale, and the spoon grip.
All movement is real-time. Do not use speed ramps, bullet time, shaky flash cuts, glow flares, or rotating camera tricks. Editing joins on action, eyeline, and the continuous crying bridge, never cutting away exactly when an expression starts to change. Color, tear tracks, clothing-fold structure, seats, and utensil states remain continuous. Off-screen bodies continue the same action state from the previous shot.

Priority order:
identity and spatial continuity > action/contact and emotional causality > readable eyes and true breathing > camera and physical detail.
Exclude face swaps, facial stretching, exaggerated mouth shapes, synchronized mechanical expressions, extra fingers or limbs, merged hands, drifting chairs, teleporting utensils, Alin’s meal appearing from nowhere, three meals collapsing into one, food suddenly appearing in an empty tray, ghost figures or reflected duplicates, subtitles, watermarks, or asset-board text. Always present one continuous lived moment of two adult women at the same table in the same room.

🎬 Long Cinematic AI Video Prompt

Prompt 

A cinematic teen drama short film, shot in warm golden-hour autumn light on the aluminum bleachers of a high school football stadium. The overall tone is naturalistic and emotionally intimate with a sudden comedic-revenge twist. Shallow depth of field, soft bokeh from sunlight hitting metal bleacher rails, handheld documentary-style camera with gentle drift, 24fps film grain, warm orange-and-teal color grade, lens flares from low sun.

**Shot 1 (0–5s):** Close-mid shot of a teenage girl with soft blonde hair pulled into a messy bun, wearing an off-shoulder cream sweater over a black tank top. She sits on metal bleachers scrolling intently on her phone. Beside her, a teenage boy in a light blue oversized hoodie with shaggy brown hair leans in close over her shoulder, peering at the screen with mild curiosity. Soft rim lighting from the setting sun behind them, blurred silver bleacher rows in the background, a few autumn leaves scattered on the seats.

**Shot 2 (5–9s):** Sudden jump cut — a burst of red smoke or colored powder explodes into frame, enveloping a small group of three teens sitting further down the bleachers. They flinch back in surprise, hands raised defensively to shield their faces, hair and loose strands whipped by the gust of the blast. Golden sunlight scatters through the red haze creating a hazy, dreamlike, slightly chaotic visual. Quick, reactive camera shake sells the surprise.

**Shot 3 (9–14s):** Intimate close-up portrait of a different girl — wavy, sunlit flyaway hair, delicate gold hoop earrings and a thin gold necklace, wearing a white knitted top. She looks down at her phone with a quiet, pensive, slightly worried expression, warm backlight haloing her hair, skin tones glowing in the low sun. The mood shifts from chaos to a quieter, tense beat.

**Shot 4 (14–20s):** Low-angle wide shot looking straight up at a bright yellow steel goalpost crossbar cutting diagonally across a clear, deep-blue late-afternoon sky. Below it, three teenagers stand on the field looking upward with concern and frustration — one boy in a grey hoodie with a black backpack reaches up and starts climbing the vertical post, straining to reach something lodged at the top. Two girls stand nearby, one with long brown hair looking up anxiously, the other in a navy striped sweater raising both hands toward the sky in a pleading/frustrated gesture. Their phones are visibly stuck on top of the crossbar. Blurred autumn-orange treeline and stadium floodlight tower visible at the edges of frame.

**Overall mood/theme:** "Messing with Amelia" backfires — a lighthearted teen revenge-prank narrative where the antagonist group's phones end up stranded on the stadium goalpost, and they're now desperately trying to climb up and fetch them. Comedic-ironic, youthful, slightly cinematic-trailer energy. Aspect ratio 1080x608, widescreen cinematic crop, subtle ambient wind/rustle sound design implied, no dialogue — purely visual storytelling with expressive reactions.

Seedance 2.5 prompt👇
Create a 25-second, 16:9, 11-shot realistic cinematic sequence in the same base shooting range, one continuous time span, with only two adult women: Alin and Lisa. No dialogue, no narration, no subtitles, no background voices.

Priority 1: Lisa begins already firing fast with obvious anger, not calm practice and not pure sadness: brows pulled inward and down, lower lids tight, jaw clenched, lips pressed thin, shoulders loaded, breath short and held. Priority 2: Alin remains completely off-screen until 05.5s, then enters and is fully set by 08.0s. Priority 3: after the handoff, Lisa must clearly hold one pistol in her right hand and the other in her left; both grips, both slides, both hands, and both forearms must remain visibly separate in character shots. Never make it look like both hands are on one gun.

Lisa is skilled and uses fast, heavy shooting to vent revenge-driven anger. Alin walks in from off-screen and gives Lisa the second pistol that had been tucked directly into Alin’s right-front waistband. Lisa takes it urgently, resists Alin’s gaze for a moment, then accepts it and resumes firing. The back half stays fast and dense; the change is internal: face shifts from clenched to loosened, motion from overforced to compact, breath from held to flowing. She ends still determined, never smiling or celebrating. All action stays real-time except the glass shatter at 20.0-21.6s, which is the only slow motion.

Reference binding:
Image 1 = Alin only: adult woman, pale blonde long straight hair with blunt bangs, white ruched camisole, blue jeans, brown belt, brown long boots, same facial structure and proportions.
Image 2 = Lisa only: adult woman, short blonde hair, orange-brown leather jacket with shearling collar, inner layer, deep brown waist cinch, short skirt, waist pouch, thigh strap, ankle boots; keep the real orange-brown color, never turn it red.
Image 3 = two identical black pistols only: same silhouette, metal finish, grip, and red-dot optic. Gun A starts in Lisa’s right hand. Gun B starts tucked directly into Alin’s right-front waistband above the beltline, no holster. Alin is off-screen at first, so gun B is also off-screen until she enters. The red-dot sight is not a laser emitter.
Image 4 = the base shooting range only: old concrete pillars, overhead pipes, warm hanging lamps, damp floor, yellow firing line, crates, rusted oil drums, bottle-and-can targets, steel plate and sandbag background, right-side corridor. Preserve the architectural depth. Exclude all board layout, labels, arrows, white background, and multi-view presentation.

Space and blocking:
Keep Image 4 layout. The target wall is north, the firing line south, the right corridor east. Lisa stands centered just south of the yellow line, facing north, and stays in the same foot zone the whole time. She can rotate slightly through the torso but never drifts sideways or walks toward the targets. Targets remain north.
Alin starts about 1.7 m southwest of Lisa, fully outside frame. Before 05.5s, no body part, reflection, or waist gun of Alin is visible. At 05.5s, after Lisa stops firing, Alin enters naturally from the rear-side frame edge, taking two normal steps along a short southwest-to-northeast path, moving about 1.1 m, then slowing to a stop about 0.6 m behind-left of Lisa. The camera must let the audience see the real entry and stop; never cut to an Alin already standing there. Gun B becomes visible only when she enters. After 08.0s both foot positions are fixed through the end. The handoff happens by natural arm reach only. Alin stays behind the firing line, never crosses Lisa’s arms, never moves to Lisa’s right side, never stands between muzzle and targets.
All human camera angles remain in the west half-space, so the shooting direction reads leftward in side views. Two-shots favor a southwest oblique angle so both faces are readable without blocking each other. Eye contact begins with the eyes, then a small head turn; torsos still face north. Guns stay lowered toward the target line during looks to the other person. In dual-gun shots, choose a shallow oblique angle that keeps the two guns visually separated; do not stack them into one silhouette or blur the far gun away.

Target continuity:
Two left cans are for the early hits. Midfield old bottle and can are for the later hits. The right green bottle is reserved only for the final hit. Target positions stay fixed. Damage accumulates: fallen cans remain down, broken bottle remnants and glass remain, and the green bottle stays intact until 20.0s. Debris never teleports to the women’s feet.

Gun-count proof, locked:
There are exactly two identical black pistols, tracked narratively as A and B, though no letters appear on screen.
00-08s: Lisa holds gun A in her right hand, left hand empty. Gun B is tucked in Alin’s right-front waistband, no holster, and remains off-screen with Alin until she enters.
08-11s: fixed medium two-shot from waist up. Lisa’s right-hand gun A is visible throughout. Alin draws gun B from her own waistband with her right hand and places it into Lisa’s empty left hand. Lisa stabilizes it, Alin releases and withdraws her now-empty hand. No tossing, flashing, or teleporting. The end of the shot must hold at least half a second proving the result: Lisa right hand = gun A, Lisa left hand = gun B, both hands and both guns separate and clear; Alin’s hands empty; Alin’s waistband empty.
11s-end: every character shot with Lisa must preserve two distinct pistols with visible spacing between hands. Both grips, both slides, and their corresponding forearms must be readable. During eye contact both guns stay low but still inside frame. When she resumes firing, each gun rises from its own hand. Lisa’s left hand always keeps gun B and never supports gun A. Gun A is never handed back, set down, or tucked away. Alin remains empty-handed after the transfer. If you cut to targets, off-screen continuity still preserves Lisa dual-wielding and Alin empty-handed. 13.0-16.6s must first show uninterrupted medium-shot dual-gun firing before any target insert. 17.3-20.0s must keep Lisa’s face and both guns in the same frame; no face-only close-up that hides the guns. 21.6-25.0s must also clearly show both guns in her hands.

Performance:
Lisa’s opening anger must read in the first second: inward-dropped brows, sharp eyes, tight lower lids, hard jawline, thin lips, loaded shoulders, held breath. This is emotional discharge, not neutral range practice. After the first burst she is still unsatisfied. The second burst is even more forceful. Even on hits her mouth stays tight. When Alin enters, Lisa only cuts her eyes first, then gives a short head turn; her body does not soften toward Alin. She takes the second gun briskly and wants to keep going immediately. Alin’s sustained gaze stops the lift for a beat. During the look, Lisa first keeps the jaw tight as if refusing to be seen, then glances away, returns to Alin, loosens the lips first, exhales longer, and only then lets the shoulders drop. This transition begins across the eye-contact beat and early second half, not instantly on contact. The first dual-gun burst still carries residue of her anger; after one short breath the jaw loosens further. She continues firing fast and dense, still focused and determined, but the mouth is no longer pressed thin and the shoulder reaction is more compact. She chooses when to stop; she is not interrupted by fear or collapse. At the end her eyes soften slightly toward Alin, then return to the targets with resolve. No smile, no sudden cheerfulness. The opening anger is absorbed into control, not erased.
Alin enters looking at the target zone, then quickly shifts to Lisa’s still-clenched face; this recognition slows her last step. Her brow tightens, jaw firms briefly, and her own pain is touched. She draws and offers the gun more steadily than Lisa moves, but without hesitation. When Lisa rushes to continue, Alin simply holds the gaze. Her lips part slightly and close again; finally she gives one exhale and a small shoulder drop. Only after Lisa begins to respond does Alin’s brow ease. During the second firing phase, Alin keeps watching seriously; only when she sees Lisa self-regulate does her slight forward lean relax. At the end she receives Lisa’s glance and gives one small nod.
Their reactions are staggered, never synchronized. Eyes lead, head follows. Keep subtle gaze shifts, natural blinks, and believable lamp reflections. Do not lock pupils or make both blink on every shot. Each shot carries only one dominant acting beat. No crying, no fresh tears, no spoken mouth shapes; lips only move with breathing. Face structure stays stable. In close shots, use smaller expression amplitude, but the difference between the tight opening face and the looser ending face must remain visible.

Rhythm and speed:
00-05.5s is rapid, weighty, continuous shooting. Do not turn it into evenly spaced shot-pause-shot timing. She is already in motion at frame one. Within a burst she does not lower the arm, check hits, or reset posture. Speed comes from short starts, chained reactions, and clean recoveries; gunshot pulses chase each other, and the next target reacts before the previous one finishes falling. The first shot contains one brief flourish between two firing bursts, but it is integrated into flow, not a pose. Real stop-fire begins only after 05.5s.
13-20s must also stay fast and dense; emotional easing must not turn into slow deliberate single shots. Build it from short intense clusters separated only by tiny breath gaps: first cluster still forceful, short breath, then a tighter compact cluster, then a clear finish. The gaps are only long enough for one short breath. Do not fake speed with global speed-up, frame skipping, sliding feet, or rubbery motion. Alin’s walk-in, the handoff, the look, and the ending all stay normal real time. 20.0-21.6s is the only slow motion.

Color and light:
Use a realistic post-apocalyptic palette: low-saturation industrial gray-brown with restrained tungsten warmth, consistent with Image 4. Palette reference only: coal black #262827 for deep structure and gun shadows; aged iron brown-gray #62574A for walls, crates, barrels; dark olive gray #505447 for backlit environment; tungsten amber #B88B55 for lamp glow and metal reflections; old ivory #D8D1C4 for the lit planes of Alin’s top. Keep Lisa’s jacket orange-brown with reduced saturation, not recolored. Preserve natural skin tone and layered blonde hair. The green bottle stays dark green and semi-translucent.
The hanging lamps are about 3000-3200K, with a viewing balance around 3800K: warm lamps, but white fabric and skin do not go yellow. The right corridor keeps only a weak neutral depth light; do not add strong blue fill. Midtones stay natural. Shadows remain dense but readable enough to see fingers, waistline, and gun bodies. Highlights roll off softly, preserving white-cloth folds, forehead texture, and glass edges. Fine grain, slight lamp bloom, no beauty smoothing, no oversharpening, no cheap teal-orange grade.
Lamp position, exposure baseline, shadow hue, black level, and grain stay consistent across shots. Warm reflections change only with real camera angle. The dark side of faces still retains eyes and lip line through environmental bounce. Muzzle flash gives only brief local warm reflections and never whites out the room. When emotion calms, the light does not brighten or warm; the change comes only through performance and framing.

Gunfire and physical effects:
Gunfire must feel like dense, pulsing handgun bursts, never like an infinite machine gun stream. Each burst has a clear start, rapid recoil chain, and recovery. Guns, forearms, and shoulders act as one weight-bearing system. Recoil is short and readable, with sleeves lagging slightly. Early overexertion appears as muscle and breath tension, not wild muzzle wagging or full-body jumping. The two pistols move independently, not in perfect sync and never fusing into one broad weapon. Firing comes in finite fast clusters, not nonstop for the whole piece. No reload or magazine-change business.
Muzzle flash is brief and restrained: warm yellow core, pale orange edge, instant fade, with occasional reflections on metal, leather, and the near face edge. No huge fireballs. Mechanical cycling stays in sync with firing. Ejected casings are small spent shells only, not live rounds. They appear briefly when angle allows, then arc, bounce, roll, and stop under inertia and gravity; never become a shower of golden particles. In normal speed, bullets are never visible in flight. No laser lines, tracers, air tunnels, or bullet-follow shots. Bullet presence is conveyed through gunfire and target reaction only.
Use a little thin gray-white muzzle smoke that rises and disperses locally, then fades after stop-fire; never let smoke hide faces or hands. Targets react only after the corresponding gunshot, never before. Cans dent, flip, strike wood, and fall; they do not explode or shatter like glass. Glass breaks from a local impact point into larger tumbling pieces and smaller shards, with believable thickness and reflections; the bottle base keeps weight. The wood stand gives only a little old dust or tiny splinters at impact points. The steel backplate shows only minimal localized reaction. No carpet of sparks.
Shot 10, the green bottle break, is the only hero slow-motion effect: the crack begins, then the shot briefly slows. Shards continue moving and falling. Their bright edges flash only while passing through the fixed warm lamp direction, then dim. No hovering, no reverse motion, no glowing powder cloud. The broken state remains afterward.
Ambient dust exists only sparingly under the lamps. Impact dust appears only at the north target stand, expands briefly, then settles or fades. Nothing sprays from skin, gun grips, or floor without cause. Floor reflections stay dark and broken, not mirror copies.

Clothing and contact physics:
Lisa’s leather jacket has thickness: quick arm lifts tighten the shoulder seams and fold the elbows; after stopping, cuffs and collar lag slightly, then settle. The waist cinch restricts large torso twist. The skirt moves only with real weight shifts, never with nonexistent wind. Waist pouch and thigh strap stay attached with slight lag, never floating. Short hair flicks lightly with head turns and settles back without hiding the eyes for long.
As Alin approaches, her jeans form weight creases at hips and knees, and her boot soles read with real contact shadow. Cut hard on action and sound continuity. Never replay the handoff or reset actions to their starting positions. Through target inserts, Lisa still owns gun A in the right hand and gun B in the left. Prompt part 1:

VISUAL STYLE

High-quality 2D Japanese action anime with expressive hand-drawn character animation, clean confident linework, flat cel shading, strong contrast, dramatic cinematic composition and consistent character designs. Traditional anime cinematography with deliberate shot changes, expressive reaction shots, exaggerated facial expressions and carefully timed comedic pauses.

The scene transitions between restrained cinematic suspense, exaggerated anime fear reactions, and an explosively animated moment of violence. Keep the quieter sections controlled and readable. Reserve the most extreme animation techniques for the desk impact.

SETTING AND CHARACTER CONTINUITY

A luxurious Japanese yakuza patriarch's office at night. Dark wooden walls, expensive furnishings and a large, heavy polished wooden desk. The patriarch sits behind his desk.

MIKA@d21d2e89-f19b-47a9-a6e0-e8a6fc511acf: Athletic professional wrestler with blonde hair, wearing her established Yakuza Wars outfit. Playful, energetic and cheerfully unhinged. She treats intimidation and violence as though they are ordinary parts of her working day.

PATRIARCH@193cf5dc-b4d4-4e55-9716-60ebf4fc6a1e: Elderly Japanese yakuza boss with slicked-back silver hair, moustache and beard, a scar across one eye, and an expensive black three-piece suit with gold accents.

BUBBLES@5a66c8bb-35c3-41a1-94f4-cf7e7997e794: A huge, muscular man in a dark suit. He is already dead when the scene begins. Mika drags his limp, motionless corpse by the head.

Exactly one Mika, one patriarch and one Bubbles. Maintain consistent character designs, clothing, office layout and screen direction throughout.

SHOT 1 — THE DOOR

Static, straight-on shot of the closed office door. The corridor is quiet. The door remains closed and motionless.

Hold the composition long enough to establish anticipation. No camera movement.

SHOT 2 — THE PATRIARCH

Cut to a medium shot of the patriarch sitting behind his desk. He looks collected, stern and self-assured. His posture is upright and composed. He waits patiently, apparently expecting an ordinary visitor.

Restrained animation. Almost imperceptible movement.

SHOT 3 — SOMETHING IS WRONG

Slow cinematic push-in to a close-up of the patriarch's face.

A bead of sweat appears at his temple and slowly runs down his face. His confident expression begins to falter. His eyes shift nervously towards the door. His mouth tightens, and his composure becomes visibly strained.

Classic anime suspense: a subtle shadow crosses his face, his eyes widen slightly, and his expression communicates mounting dread.

SHOT 4 — THE ENTRANCE

The office door is suddenly kicked violently inward.

A forceful impact, a burst of dust and splinters, and a brief camera shake. The door swings open with tremendous force. A thick dust cloud fills the doorway, briefly obscuring whoever entered.

Use a sudden hard cut and a sharp visual jolt to contrast with the preceding stillness.

SHOT 5 — THE REVEAL

The dust slowly settles.

Mika stands in the doorway, grinning cheerfully. She is holding Bubbles' corpse by the head with one hand. His enormous body hangs limp and drags along the floor behind her.

Mika strolls casually into the office, dragging the dead man behind her as though carrying an inconvenient piece of luggage.

The patriarch is visible deeper in the room, staring in disbelief.

The contrast is deliberate: Mika is relaxed and almost playful; the corpse is completely motionless; the patriarch's confidence is evaporating.

SHOT 6 — DISPOSING OF THE EVIDENCE

Cut to a high, angled camera looking down towards the patriarch's desk.

Mika casually swings Bubbles' limp body forward and throws him onto the floor directly in front of the desk.

His heavy body lands with a powerful THUD. His limbs flop naturally with the momentum. Dust rises slightly from the floor.

Mika barely acknowledges the body after dropping it. The patriarch is forced to look down at the corpse lying before him.

SHOT 7 — THE MESSAGE

Cut to a medium shot of Mika facing the patriarch across the desk.

Mika smiles brightly and speaks in casual, conversational English:

"Got a message from the prin— I mean, カンヅキ様."

She almost says the wrong name, catches herself halfway through, and corrects it. The delivery is natural and slightly awkward, as though she has just remembered the proper wording.

She is not shouting. She is not visibly angry. She is simply delivering a message.

SHOT 8 — ABSOLUTE TERROR

Cut to the patriarch.

He is visibly shaking in his chair. His shoulders tremble, his hands grip the arms of his chair, and his eyes are wide with terror. Sweat pours down his face. His mouth quivers as he stares at Mika.

Use exaggerated anime fear language: trembling outlines, tiny pupils, a pale face, tense shoulders, sweat droplets and subtle vibrating motion lines.

His expression communicates that he genuinely believes he is about to die. He cannot find the words to respond.

Hold the shot briefly to let the fear register.

SHOT 9 — THE DESK SLAM

Cut back to Mika in a medium shot across the desk.

Without warning, Mika leans forward over the desk and rapidly grabs the patriarch by the back of his head and hair.

Her cheerful expression barely changes.

The motion is sudden, explosive and brutally fast. This is the scene's major animation set piece.

Mika violently drives his face down into the polished wooden desk.

Use exaggerated hand-drawn anime action choreography:

A sharp, rapid movement into the grab, followed by an explosive downward acceleration.

Extreme perspective and foreshortening as the patriarch's head is driven towards the desk.

Several fast smear drawings that stretch the movement into an almost instantaneous downward strike.

Bold black speed lines converging on the exact point of impact.

A brief, high-contrast black-and-white impact frame, followed by a single deep-red accent frame.

An extreme, stylised contact frame that communicates the force of the collision.

A violent full-frame camera shake synchronised precisely with the impact.

Papers leap into the air, small desk objects jump, and the desk visibly rattles from the force.

A dramatic burst of stylised blood splatters across the polished desk at the instant of impact.

Rapid return to normal colour and detailed cel animation as Mika maintains her grip and the patriarch's body recoils.

The impact should feel like a sudden, shocking blow from a mature action anime: forceful, visually unmistakable and dramatically exaggerated. The smear frames and impact frames must be brief accents within otherwise coherent animation, not a prolonged abstract montage.

Keep the camera and character positions readable. The patriarch is struck against the desk directly in front of Mika. Mika remains standing on the opposite side of the desk, controlling the movement.

After the impact, his upper body slumps forward against the desk.

SHOT 10 — THE THREAT, A LITTLE LATE

Mika releases him and straightens up to her full height.

She adopts a confident, intimidating stance and delivers the line with theatrical emphasis:

"THIS IS カンヅキ TERRITORY!"

Her voice is suddenly loud and menacing, as though she is finally performing the dramatic threat she was supposed to deliver.

Hold the pose for a brief beat.

Mika turns away from the desk and strolls towards the exit, humming happily to herself.

She is entirely unconcerned with what she has done. Her posture is relaxed and her mood is cheerful, as though she has just finished an ordinary errand.

The camera remains fixed on the patriarch, slumped motionless over his desk in the foreground. Mika gradually walks out of frame.

Hold on the silent office, the bloodstained desk and the unresponsive patriarch after Mika has left.

End the shot on the uncomfortable contrast between the horrific scene and Mika's cheerful departure.

PACING AND SOUND DESIGN GUIDANCE

The first three shots are quiet, slow and suspenseful. The door's violent entrance breaks that stillness.

Mika's entrance and delivery of the message are deliberately casual. The patriarch's fear should build visibly before the desk slam.

The first desk slam receives the most elaborate animation, with tightly synchronised impact frames, smears, camera shake, environmental reactions and a stylised blood splash.

The dialogue after the slam is paced for dark comedy. Leave brief pauses after the territorial threat, after Mika realises her mistake, and after asking whether the patriarch heard her.

The final head drop is much smaller and more anticlimactic than the first impact.

Maintain a consistent high-quality 2D cel-shaded anime style throughout. No 3D CGI, no live-action realism, no unnecessary extra characters, no character duplication, no random camera transitions, no unintelligible dialogue, and no changes to character appearance.

Mika voice characteristics: Mika is a young lady and former professional wrestler, exuberant, playful and over-the-top. She speaks with a slight southern accent. She is always playing to a crowd even if one isn't there.

Character consistency: Maintain the established character designs throughout the scene. Mika has blood running from her nose and mouth, with visible bruising around her stomach and ribs. Bubbles is not wearing sunglasses; blood is visible around his nose and mouth. Keep these injuries, facial features, hairstyles, clothing and body proportions consistent across every shot.

Him:@fc404444-65b6-4970-9377-55371654d013 A tall, lanky, laid-back man with a long face, a big expressive nose, sleepy half-lidded amber eyes, thick dark arched eyebrows, messy dark curly hair streaked with grey, round gold-framed green-tinted goggles pushed up on his head, a salt-and-pepper goatee and mustache, big ears with gold hoop earrings, layered thin necklaces with a small pendant, a cream textured jacket with a fuzzy collar and white shearling cuffs, a small red pin on the pocket, a white ribbed tee, wide brown cuffed corduroy-style trousers, braided leather bracelets, silver rings, tan suede strap sandals with white socks. A slow cinematic glide through the sunlit apartment, with curtains billowing and dust motes floating. In the corner by the bookshelf, the cat lies curled up and fast asleep on top of the robot vacuum in its dock. The vacuum's amber eye blinks open. It gives a tiny chirp, backs out of the dock with the cat still asleep on its back, and rolls into the room. The vacuum gains speed and rolls across the rug. The cat slowly opens one eye, sits up like a captain at the helm and adjusts its scarf. Her gasps, points and jumps up, her bag swinging. Him lifts his goggles with one slow finger, blinks twice and then sits upright in surprise.

SFX: A rising whirr, a playful pizzicato run, a cat's tiny "mrrp", a surprised gasp.

SCENE 3 – THE CHASE BEGINS (6–10 SECONDS)

A low floor-level tracking shot follows the vacuum as it slides around the legs of the coffee table, whips between the sofa and the carved side tables, and curves around a stack of books. The cat leans into the turns with its scarf flying. Her sprints in close pursuit. Him follows with long, loping strides and flailing arms.

SFX: Fast bouncy strings, rapid wheel whirrs, quick footsteps, the sandals' flap-flap-flap, a happy chirp.

SCENE 4 – THE OBSTACLE COURSE (10–14 SECONDS)

The vacuum zips under the wooden laundry rack, and soft clothes sway and flutter. A sock falls over Him's face and the cat bats at another. The vacuum then slaloms through the line of shoes by the hallway door, knocking one over like a bowling pin. Him slides across the wooden floor in his socks and sandals with his legs split wide, and his goggles drop onto his eyes.

SFX: A cloth swish, a bouncy xylophone run, shoes tumbling, a long comedic slide squeak, a trombone "wah".

SCENE 5 – THE RACETRACK (14–18 SECONDS)

Signature shot. A dramatic low-angle floor-level tracking shot turns the apartment into a racetrack. Golden bars of sunlight cut across the wooden floor, the rug becomes a dirt track and the book stacks become chicanes. The vacuum hits the edge of a book pile like a ramp and launches into slow motion. Dust motes hang in the air, the cat's scarf floats and its ears flatten calmly. It lands on the rug with a soft bounce and zooms on.

SFX: Time slows with a soft low hum and gentle chimes, a swoosh in the air, a soft landing thump, then the fast music returns.

SCENE 6 – THE CORNER TRAP (18–22 SECONDS)

The vacuum heads for the corner by the bed. Him and Her split up and approach from opposite sides, arms wide, and at the same moment they both lunge and bump into each other. They tumble onto the rug in a tangle of limbs. The vacuum stops on its own at the wall, its eye dims to a small guilty amber, and it gives a sad little chirp. The cat yawns.

SFX: Music building then stopping, a soft bump, a cushioned thud, a tiny sad "boop", a gentle yawn.

SCENE 7 – THE SWEET PARKING (22–25 SECONDS)

Calm and warm. The vacuum rolls back across the rug and parks neatly between his sandals and her sneakers as they lie on the rug laughing. The cat curls up on its back, tucks in its paws and falls asleep. The vacuum's eye dims to a soft sleepy glow. Him and Her look at each other and smile, and Her rests her head on his arm. Finish with a warm close-up of the sleeping cat on the vacuum, with golden sunlight and curtains drifting gently behind it.

SFX: Soft acoustic guitar, quiet laughter fading, a gentle purr, the vacuum's soft power-down tone and a warm closing note.

- Beautiful close-ups, low-angle tracking shots and medium-wide shots.

AUDIO DESIGN

Warm, playful acoustic score with guitar, pizzicato strings, xylophone and a soft trombone for comedy beats. Small mechanical chirps for the vacuum. The slow-motion jump has a gentle hush with chimes, and the ending is soft and affectionate.

NEGATIVE: no neon or fluorescent colors, no extra characters, no logo or text on screen, no changes to the characters' faces or outfits, no scary or aggressive robot behavior, no realistic photo style.

FORMAT:
16:9 widescreen, 4K, 24fps, total duration 30 seconds. Premium cinematic action, photorealistic, grounded but surreal. Fast close-quarter silat, strong physical impacts, one brief slow motion beat, dynamic camera movement, rich environmental detail, subtle film grain.

WORLD:
A small late-night Jakarta street warung attached to an older ruko. Narrow interior with plastic chairs, metal tables, hanging snacks, instant noodle shelves, bottled drinks, cigarette display, a glass jar of crackers, a rice cooker, a small fan, cheap fluorescent lights, slightly wet tiled floor, cluttered but realistic. Outside the warung is a narrow Jakarta street with parked motorbikes, messy cables, dim streetlights, and humid night air after light rain.

CHARACTER 01:
Lean adult Indonesian man in a dark jacket, plain t-shirt, cargo pants, sneakers. Alert, tense, compact movement, practical street-fight energy.

CHARACTER 02:
Lean adult Indonesian man in a faded overshirt, dark trousers, sandals. Calm but dangerous, quick reflexes, compact silat-inspired movement.

PRIMARY SURREAL RULE:
The first half of the fight is normal.
At the first major impact, gravity inside the warung shifts 90 degrees.
This is not a visual effect only.
The environment physically reorients.
Objects slide and fall sideways.
The fighters must adapt instantly and continue fighting on the wall and tilted surfaces.
The camera remains visually readable and cinematic, not chaotic.

STORY BEAT:
A tense confrontation in a cramped Jakarta warung becomes a surreal gravity-bending fight.

0:00–0:04
Start inside the warung.
Character 01 steps in from the street, breathing slightly hard.
Character 02 is already inside near a metal table, watching him.
The fan hums, fluorescent lights buzz, distant Jakarta traffic outside.
No dialogue yet.
Strong tension.

0:04–0:07
Character 01 says quietly:
“You took the wrong thing.”
Character 02 answers:
“Then come take it back.”
They circle one another in the cramped space.
Camera moves slowly between hanging snack packs and table edges, building pressure.

0:07–0:11
First physical exchange.
A fast shove.
A wrist trap.
Short elbow.
A glass jar rattles.
A chair scrapes across the floor.
Keep the movement compact, believable, and aggressive.
No wasted motion.

0:11–0:14
Character 01 throws a hard right palm strike into Character 02’s chest.
At the moment of impact, the entire warung experiences a gravity shift.
The room rotates 90 degrees.
Chairs, cups, snack packs, a spoon jar, and loose objects slide and fall sideways.
The fighters lose balance for a split second.

0:14–0:18
They recover instantly and continue fighting on what is now effectively the wall.
Character 02 grabs a shelf edge to stabilize himself and counters with a low kick.
Character 01 catches the motion, slams Character 02 into a sideways table.
The camera tilts with the new gravity orientation but stays readable.
The warung now feels impossible yet physical.

0:18–0:22
Fast silat exchange in the gravity-shifted room.
Palm strike.
Parry.
Forearm block.
Shoulder redirect.
Short knee.
Character 01 uses a hanging rack for leverage.
Character 02 pushes off a tilted wall.
A packet display tears loose and floats briefly before dropping sideways with the new gravity.

0:22–0:25
Hero moment.
Both fighters launch toward each other at the same time.
A simultaneous strike nearly lands.
Enter a brief micro slow motion beat.
Dust, instant noodle crumbs, droplets from a tipped drink, and hanging snack wrappers suspend in the air.
Their bodies twist through the warped space.
Hold the slow motion under one second.

0:25–0:28
Snap back to real time.
Character 01 lands a hard redirect and sends Character 02 sliding across the tilted wall toward the warung entrance.
Character 02 stops himself by grabbing the doorframe.
The outside Jakarta street is now visible behind him at a bizarre angle.

0:28–0:30
Gravity suddenly snaps back to normal.
Everything drops.
Tables slam down.
Chairs hit the floor.
Loose items crash.
Both fighters land back on the real floor and freeze for one beat, facing each other.
Camera slowly pulls back through the warung entrance, revealing the cramped Jakarta street outside.
Hard cut to black.

CAMERA:
ARRI Alexa 35 cinematic look.
28mm and 35mm lens language.
Begin with tight, intimate tracking inside the cramped warung.
Use subtle handheld energy during the confrontation.
At the gravity shift, camera adapts with a controlled tilt and reorientation.
Keep motion dynamic but readable.
One brief micro slow motion beat only.
Final move is a smooth pullback out of the entrance.

FIGHT PERFORMANCE:
Compact silat-inspired street fight.
No wide superhero swings.
No exaggerated wire-fu flips.
Efficient palm strikes, elbows, traps, knees, short kicks, redirects, grabs.
The choreography must stay clear and brutal.

NATIVE AUDIO:
No background music.
No score.

Fluorescent light buzz.
Small electric fan hum.
Distant Jakarta traffic.
Motorbike passing outside.
Table scrape.
Plastic chair drag.
Glass rattle.
Snack pack rustle.
Fabric movement.
Body impacts.
Footsteps on tile.
Objects crashing during the gravity shift.
Short heavy breathing.
The line delivery should sound natural and low-key.

VISUAL STYLE:
Photorealistic cinematic realism.
Humid Jakarta night.
Natural fluorescent and street lighting.
Slight wet reflections.
Cluttered authentic warung texture.
No cyberpunk palette.
No neon sci-fi worldbuilding.
Keep it grounded, dirty, tactile, and physical.

NEGATIVE DIRECTION:
No comedy acting.
No exaggerated anime facial reactions.
No superhero poses.
No floating energy beams.
No magical glowing aura.
No impossible acrobatics.
No gore.

"OBJETIVO
Crear un video cinematográfico de 30 segundos, con tono de parodia épica y tierna, inspirado en la escena clásica de Don Quijote y Sancho contra el molino, pero protagonizado por gatitos. Debe sentirse coherente, fluido y muy consistente entre planos.
REFERENCIAS DE PERSONAJES
Usa únicamente las hojas de personaje adjuntas como referencia visual obligatoria para mantener identidad, vestuario, proporciones y estilo.
[Hoja de personaje 1] Don Quijote gatito caballero. Gatito pequeño grisáceo, armadura de caballero, casco con visera levantada, capa clara, lanza larga estilo Don Quijote. Debe conservar exactamente su diseño de la hoja de personaje.
[Hoja de personaje 2] Sancho Panza gatito escudero. Gatito pequeño, naranja y gordete, con gorro campesino, ropa humilde y bastón. Debe conservar exactamente su diseño de la hoja de personaje.
[Hoja de personaje 3] Ficha de monturas. Don Quijote cabalga el burrito ligeramente más alto. Sancho cabalga el burrito algo más bajo y compacto.
ESTILO VISUAL Y TONO
Cinematográfico, realista pero adorable, con acabado de película. Los gatitos deben verse pequeños y expresivos, con movimiento creíble. Los burritos deben verse algo más realistas que caricaturescos. Tono de parodia tierna, épica y levemente dramática. Sin diálogo. La narración se apoya en actuación, encuadre y timing cómico.
ENTORNO Y ATMÓSFERA
Paisaje inspirado en La Mancha: camino de tierra o sendero rural serpenteante, colinas suaves, terreno seco, pasto amarillento, tierra clara, piedras, horizonte amplio, aire castellano, luz natural. Puede haber una fortaleza o construcciones lejanas muy discretas si ayuda al ambiente, pero no deben verse molinos al inicio ni en los primeros planos. Los molinos deben permanecer ocultos hasta el momento del gag final.
Luz de tarde suave, ligeramente dorada pero no excesiva. Ambiente abierto, algo de viento en el paisaje. El viento debe cobrar más fuerza en el momento heroico de Don Quijote.
REGLAS DE CONSISTENCIA
Mantener el mismo lugar, misma hora del día, misma dirección de la luz y misma continuidad espacial en todos los planos.
Don Quijote siempre va delante y sobre el burrito ligeramente más alto.
Sancho siempre va detrás o un poco más retrasado, sobre el burrito más pequeño.
Don Quijote porta una lanza, no una espada.
Sancho lleva su bastón.
Mantener el mismo diseño exacto de personajes, vestuario, armadura, ropajes y monturas en todos los planos.
No mostrar molinos antes del choque. Solo debe verse el molino después del impacto.
Las transiciones deben sentirse cinematográficas, con cortes limpios y continuidad de dirección.
La comicidad debe surgir del contraste entre la épica de Don Quijote y la realidad del golpe contra el molino.
ESTRUCTURA TEMPORAL EXACTA
Duración total: 30 segundos.
0:00 - 0:05
Plano lateral medio, composición similar a una silueta de Don Quijote y Sancho avanzando de perfil por el camino. Don Quijote va delante sobre su burrito, Sancho detrás en el suyo. Ambos cabalgan tranquilos y cansados. Sancho transmite agotamiento. No se ven molinos. Movimiento suave, paso lento, ambiente sereno.
0:05 - 0:08
Don Quijote se detiene en seco. Su burrito frena. Corte a un primer plano o plano medio corto de Don Quijote deteniendo la montura y mirando fijamente al horizonte con su carita pequeña y muy seria. Debe sentirse que ha percibido algo importante.
0:08 - 0:11
Plano de Sancho. Sancho se ve contrariado y confundido. No entiende por qué se han detenido. Baja torpemente del burrito, todavía cansado, mirando a Don Quijote con desconcierto.
0:11 - 0:15
Plano de Don Quijote ya en el suelo. Ha desmontado. Avanza unos pasos con solemnidad, caminando con su lanza. Entonces una sombra enorme empieza a cubrirlo desde arriba o desde un lado. Cuando la sombra lo cubre por completo, se detiene.
0:15 - 0:18
Plano heroico de Don Quijote. Se planta recto y quieto, con la lanza erguida, en una pose épica y decidida, inspirada en la pose frontal de su hoja de personaje. El viento sopla con fuerza y hace ondear sutilmente su capa y su pelaje. Debe sentirse como un momento grandioso, exageradamente heroico y un poco ridículo a la vez.
0:18 - 0:22
Primer plano o plano medio corto de Don Quijote en posición de ataque. Se tensa, baja ligeramente el centro de gravedad y arranca de golpe a embestir con toda la determinación del mundo hacia algo que todavía no vemos. La cámara no revela aún el objetivo.
0:22 - 0:26
Plano del impacto. Don Quijote embiste con la lanza contra una pared blanca de molino de viento. El choque es súbito y cómico. Rebota con violencia caricaturesca pero físicamente clara, cae boca arriba al suelo y queda inmóvil unos instantes, como si hubiera perdido el conocimiento.
0:26 - 0:28
Plano más abierto. Ahora sí se revela claramente que Don Quijote está tendido en el suelo, diminuto, delante de un molino de viento blanco tradicional manchego, similar a los de Campo de Criptana. El molino debe verse por primera vez aquí. Sancho puede aparecer al fondo o acercándose, pero sin robar protagonismo.
0:28 - 0:30
Plano final de Sancho, negando con la cabeza, frustrado y contrariado. Debe cerrar con una nota cómica, tierna y digna. Fin.
LENGUAJE DE CÁMARA
Usar lenguaje de cámara cinematográfico y limpio.
Priorizar planos medios, primeros planos expresivos y un plano abierto final para el reveal del molino.
Mantener continuidad lateral clara.
Evitar movimientos de cámara exagerados o caóticos.
Los cortes deben ser elegantes y narrativos.
ACCIÓN Y ACTUACIÓN
Don Quijote debe actuar como un héroe diminuto, serio, idealista y valiente.
Sancho debe actuar como compañero leal, cansado, prudente y confundido.
La actuación facial de ambos debe ser muy importante.
El gag debe sentirse claro: Don Quijote interpreta una amenaza épica donde en realidad hay un molino.
PROMPT MAESTRO
Genera un video cinematográfico de 30 segundos, consistente entre planos, basado en la parodia tierna y épica de Don Quijote y Sancho contra el molino, protagonizada por gatitos. Usa exclusivamente las hojas de personaje adjuntas como referencia obligatoria para Don Quijote gatito caballero, Sancho gatito escudero y sus dos burritos. Mantén exactamente los diseños, vestuario, armadura, ropajes y monturas de las referencias.

10. EVITAR
No mostrar molinos antes del golpe.
No cambiar el diseño de los personajes entre planos.
No volver caricaturescos los burritos.
No hacer movimientos de cámara exagerados.
No introducir elementos modernos.

Flowers throughout: marigold and jasmine garlands strung across streets and temple doorways, lotus offerings, rangoli kolam patterns at entrances, rose and marigold petals falling through the air, flower sellers with heaped baskets.

SCENE-BY-SCENE (30 seconds)
Scene 1 (0–4s), The river and the city reveal @[Image 1](image_1) (Tungabhadra / boulder landscape)
The drone rises slowly over the Tungabhadra River at sunrise. Round coracle boats carry pilgrims with flower baskets across the water. The camera tilts up to reveal the vast golden boulder hills and the sprawling city beyond, smoke from temple lamps drifting upward.

Scene 2 (4–8s), Virupaksha Temple worship @[Image 3](image_3): ( Virupaksha gopuram and courtyard)
The drone glides toward the towering painted gopuram of Virupaksha Temple, hung with marigold garlands. It descends into the courtyard, where hundreds of devotees offer flowers and coconuts, priests wave brass aarti lamps, bells ring, and petals scatter in the air.

Scene 3 (8–13s), Hampi Bazaar, gems and gold @[Image 7](image_7) (: Hampi Bazaar / pillared street mandapas)
The camera tracks low down the long colonnaded bazaar street. Merchants under the stone mandapas display open heaps of rubies, emeralds, diamonds and pearls on silk cloths, measuring gems on brass scales. Goldsmiths craft necklaces at small anvils. Traders from Persia and Portugal in foreign dress bargain with local merchants. The street is packed with shoppers, flower sellers, spice and silk stalls, and cotton awnings in saffron and red.

Scene 4 (13–18s), Royal elephants (@[Image 6](image_6): Elephant Stables)
The drone sweeps past the domed Elephant Stables as a line of royal war elephants walks out. They are decorated with gold-embroidered caparisons, brass bells, painted foreheads, and silver howdahs, with mahouts seated on their necks. Children throw flower petals as they pass.

Scene 5 (18–23s), Soldiers and cavalry (@[Image 4](image_4): Mahanavami Dibba / royal enclosure)
A wide aerial view of the royal enclosure and the great stone Mahanavami platform. Columns of Vijayanagara soldiers march in formation with spears, curved swords and round shields, wearing red and white tunics. Cavalry on Arabian horses with ornate saddles and plumes trot in disciplined rows. The king watches from the decorated platform under a white royal parasol.

Scene 6 (23–27s), The Vittala Temple and stone chariot (@[Image 8](image_8): Vittala Temple / Stone Chariot)
The drone circles the carved Stone Chariot in the Vittala Temple courtyard. Musicians tap the musical pillars, dancers in silk perform in the mandapa, and devotees carry flower offerings. Garlands hang from every pillar as oil lamps begin to glow.

Scene 7 (27–30s), Grand finale (@[Image 9](image_9): Hemakuta Hill / sunset panorama)
The drone pulls back and rises high above Hemakuta Hill at sunset, revealing the entire glowing city of Vijayanagara: temple towers, bustling bazaars, the river and a procession of elephants and horsemen winding through the streets. Thousands of lamps light up as the camera slowly fades into a golden sky.

p:
Cinematic vertical sci-fi short, 36 seconds. A silver-haired man in a long black coat with ornate gold circular clockwork embroidery, with a small squirrel on his shoulder, travels through time inside a shimmering transparent bubble. The world around him jumps through eras: a burning, smoky primeval forest, a glowing sunset city seen from a hillside, an arctic ice field under a starry sky, a green wetland with mountains, and a pristine utopian city at golden hour. Cut to a short-cropped blonde woman in a sleek black dress watching a futuristic organic-architecture city, with white spiral towers and giant petal-shaped trees, flourish at sunrise. The man steps out of the bubble onto a glass walkway streaked with glowing orange and teal light lines, bursts through a sparkling energy explosion, and arrives in the future. A crowd of elegantly dressed people in muted earth tones, plus a woman in a pale silver gown, waits on the bridge. Warm golden-hour light, lens flares, shallow depth of field, soft atmospheric haze, epic yet calm mood, slow gliding camera, photoreal, high-end sci-fi film look, 9:16, 30fps.
Shot-by-shot version (better control):
Forest fire: Dark, smoky forest, embers glowing, slow drift forward. Time-lapse feel.
Woman on the balcony: Medium shot, blonde woman in a black dress raises a hand toward a futuristic city at golden hour. Birds fly across the sky, camera orbits slowly.
Bubble, sunset: Low-angle hero shot of the man in the clockwork coat inside a glass bubble, with a city of lights glowing behind him.
Light bridge: Woman stands on a reflective walkway with streaking orange and teal light lines, giant petal-trees behind her.
Bubble, ice age: Man looks up at the starry sky on an ice field, bubble shimmering.
Bubble, wetlands: Rear shot of the man looking over green wetlands and mountains, squirrel on his shoulder.
Bubble, haze: Soft pastel haze, the bubble starts to dissolve.
Bubble, utopia: The bubble lands on a glass bridge, with a utopian skyline and spheres on towers behind him.
Burst: The man sprints forward through an explosion of golden sparks and light streaks, the bubble bursting around him.
Arrival: He slows to a walk and meets the waiting crowd, then the woman in the pale gown steps forward, the camera pushing in gently.

时长 15 秒，24fps；风格：90 年代日式赛璐璐手绘 + 粗粝美漫笔触 + 低饱和度 NPR 三渲二，复古太空西部 + 黑色爵士电影质感。清晰墨线、硬边大阴影，哑光金属 + 旧皮革材质，画面带手绘磨损、胶片颗粒。布光：左上暖琥珀吊灯主光，舷窗射入冷蓝星光。人物动作带 12fps 手绘质感，爆发动作配短拖影、接触强调，镜头跟随实体位移。主角机械面罩固定，靠头倾角、帽檐、肩与机械手指传递情绪。
场景：殖民星轨道港老式酒吧，左窄吧台、右侧圆弧卡座，卡座旁黑胶唱机；圆形舷窗外悬浮巨大土黄色行星，破旧货船缓慢入港。环境布满仪表、磨损皮革、钨丝灯，充满使用痕迹。角色：少言快枪、拮据机械赏金猎人（枪初始在右腰枪套）；对手是穿棕旧飞行夹克的逃犯。
00:12.5–00:15｜平视镜头缓慢后拉，从中景拉全景。唱机再次停转，牛仔手指悬停，低头，帽檐遮住面光，氛围感落寞；画面收进逃犯、唱机、窗外行星，货船持续进港，归于安静。分镜时序：00:00–00:01｜低机位面部特写，短促推镜。枪口抵牛仔帽檐旁，紫面光平稳，双指扶正歪掉的帽子，头部微转，爵士贝斯铺垫。00:01–00:03｜吧台高度中全景，侧移拉开镜头。牛仔松弛坐高脚凳，逃犯在身后持枪对峙；牛仔右手移向枪套，手指轻敲台面，后景行星与货船入镜。00:03–00:03.5｜平视固定特写，黑胶转动、唱针震颤，浮尘在暖光里飘动，萨克斯起调。00:03.5–00:04.5｜低机位胸部近景轻推。牛仔停手，侧头：“先听完这首。” 同时左脚踩实、右脚勾凳、右手扣枪柄。00:04.5–00:07｜低机位微斜，横向快跟拍。逃犯开枪，牛仔侧滑落地，子弹擦帽檐打在横梁溅起火星；手撑吧台横移，踢凳子绊倒逃犯，近身缠斗。00:07–00:10｜腰高机位跟转中全景。牛仔拔枪顶开对方手臂，揪住衣领将逃犯甩进卡座，撞落手枪，磁锁手铐锁在卡座扶手；震动震跳唱针，音乐卡壳重复短音。00:10–00:12.5｜平视中近景短推。牛仔收枪，按住逃犯，机械双指轻敲唱机外壳，音乐续上旋律，肩膀随节拍微动。
声画设定：内声源 Bebop 爵士，行走贝斯、刷镲、萨克斯；音效：机械指节声、枪响、凳刮地面、手铐咔锁声；音乐随唱针卡顿断续，片尾静音，仅舱体嗡鸣、风扇声、逃犯喘息。仅一句台词，无字幕旁白。

云山竹林间的古木茶庐，竹格窗有冷白侧逆光，炉火给木纹添一点暖色。榆木案上只有一只青瓷茶盏，盛半盏澄亮琥珀茶汤。她想图省事，用一个小火诀把冷茶温一温。两手空着，施法全靠手诀。

0–1.3 秒｜贴案微距拍完全静止的冷茶，茶面清晰，无热汽。她疲倦平淡的脸在后方柔焦。轻轻移焦，切同侧近景。她举右手至胸前，食指中指并拢，拇指扣住屈起的无名指和小指，掐出干净的双指火诀。左手仍搭在桌沿。

1.3–3.6 秒｜越肩特写同时看清两根指尖、空气间隙、青瓷盏和茶面。她双指向杯心斜下方轻点一次，指尖亮起一点朱红橙金的小灵火；一缕短而细的火息从指尖出发，掠过空气，明确触到茶汤正中央，触点才亮起细小暖光。接触前茶汤不动；接触后茶汤先起涟漪、再缓慢旋转。半秒后，茶面先冒一丝淡白水汽，随温度升高变成两三缕清晰上升的半透明白汽，窗光照亮卷曲边缘。俯拍见旋转加快到一个受控的小漩涡，少量气泡和茶珠只在杯口内，杯外干净。

3.6–4.7 秒｜她眼睛略睁大，立即一屈双指、收掌灭诀。火光瞬间熄灭，水旋即停。画面明确留出半拍，拍同一盏已经平静的茶仍往上冒着白色热汽。蒸汽从液面自然升起，被室内微风带向窗边；没有火苗和烟灰。

4.7–6.1 秒｜同轴近三分之四侧面。她神情平淡，用双手把还在冒白汽的同一只青瓷盏举到唇边，盏口始终托在嘴唇正下方。镜头同时清楚拍到嘴、杯沿和杯口。

6.1–7.0 秒｜正常速度，维持同一个近侧特写，嘴与杯口都看得见。她只轻啜一小口。热茶刚碰舌尖，她就缩眉，杯沿反射性向下撤约四厘米，杯口仍正对嘴下方。杯沿离唇的下一瞬，她立刻“噗”地吐出刚入口的茶，几颗明显的琥珀茶滴从嘴唇飞过这段空隙，准确打在原盏的茶面上，激起一圈小涟漪。短促、干脆、清晰，嘴到杯口的路径完整可见，白汽飘向窗侧。反应与吐出紧接，停顿只在茶滴落杯之后。

7.0–10 秒｜吐完才停。她缓缓呼气，神情由烫到的紧绷松开，安静而难以置信地盯着杯子，把杯子往案上放。热茶仍向窗侧飘出清楚的半透明白汽，最后在杯子下放途中结束。人物不笑、不看镜头。

A miniature bathroom with warm cream tiles, a pale stone vanity, and soft diffused morning daylight. Uncluttered background. Eye-level frontal framing with clear views of the hands and face.

Exactly 15 seconds. Brisk, playful pacing with clean cuts between actions. Use natural-speed movements and short, readable gestures rather than speeding up the footage.

She makes two quick circular rubbing motions across her cheeks, spreading abundant dense, fine white foam over her entire face: forehead, cheeks, nose, and chin.

Her left hand steadies the bottle while her right hand unscrews its short-threaded dropper cap and lifts out the attached glass pipette vertically.
